{"Docs":[{"DocType":1,"IsAmended":false,"IsUpdated":false,"CompareStatus":4,"DocOrderId":470,"AmendedBy":[],"Notes":[],"Drafts":[],"ChunkGroupStartingNodeId":"TIT5KUDERECO_CH8ZOCO_PT5ZODI","NodeDepth":4,"TitleHtml":"
5-8-501: - ZONING DISTRICTS ESTABLISHED; PURPOSE:
","ShouldShowMiniToc":false,"Id":"TIT5KUDERECO_CH8ZOCO_PT5ZODI_5-8-501ZODIESPU","Title":"5-8-501: - ZONING DISTRICTS ESTABLISHED; PURPOSE:","Content":"
\n

\n The city has established five (5) zoning districts; these being: agriculture, residential,\n commercial, manufacturing/industrial and public; additionally, the city has established\n certain overlay districts whose purposes are also identified in Part 3 of this chapter.\n \n

\n A.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Agriculture:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Agriculture district (A): The A district has been established to preserve, protect\n and assure the continuing viability of agricultural lands within the city and the\n area of city impact (ACI). This district has been established to lessen the encroachment\n of urban type development into agricultural areas whose presence would interfere with\n agricultural pursuits.\n

\n

\n Land uses, other than those directly relating to agriculture, or those typically coexisting\n with agricultural uses, are generally prohibited in this district. The agricultural\n district requires land parcels to be a minimum five (5) acres in area with certain\n exceptions.\n

\n

\n The A district refers to land uses engaged for farming, dairying, pasturage, agriculture,\n horticulture, floriculture, viticulture, animal and poultry husbandry and the accompanying\n accessory uses for packing, treating or storing the produce. Agricultural accessory\n uses shall be considered a use secondary to the normal agricultural activities. Agriculture\n does not include the operation or maintenance of a commercial stockyard or feed yard\n where large numbers of livestock are fed concentrated feeds particularly for the purpose\n of fatting for market (CAFO).\n

\n \n

\n B.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Residential:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Low density residential district (R-2): The purpose of the R-2 district is to promote\n the establishment of low-density residential areas that do not exceed two (2) dwelling\n units per net acre. The district is considered semi-rural in nature and intended to\n preserve residential living arrangements that are rural or semi-agriculture in character.\n The district serves as a transitional buffer between rural areas and higher density\n urban development. The R-2 zone is not intended to provide a full range of urban services.\n A district requirement is connection to public sewer and water with some limited exceptions\n found in KCC § 5-9-603. The R-2 zone is intended to accommodate accessory dwelling\n units [ADU], senior housing, bed and breakfast operations, single-family dwellings,\n duplexes, home occupations, manufactured homes and a limited number of agricultural\n uses. It is not intended for placement of more intensive type residential uses associated\n with condominiums, townhouses, apartments, multifamily or group living arrangements.\n

\n

\n Medium density residential district (R-4): The purpose of the R-4 district is to promote\n the development of residential living areas with low to moderate densities, not to\n exceed four (4) dwelling units per net acre. A district requirement is connection\n to public sewer and water. The district is intended to accommodate accessory dwelling\n units, bed and breakfast operations, single-family dwellings, duplexes, senior housing\n and manufactured homes. There is an opportunity to initiate mixed-use activity in\n this zone through the planned unit development (PUD) process.\n

\n

\n Medium density residential district (R-6): The purpose of the R-6 district is to promote\n the development of medium density living areas, not to exceed six (6) dwelling units\n per net acre. A district requirement is connection to public sewer and water. The\n zone is intended to accommodate single-family dwellings, duplexes, manufactured homes\n and group living arrangements. There is an opportunity to initiate mixed-use activity\n in this zone through the PUD process.\n

\n

\n High density residential district (R-8): The purpose of the R-8 district is to promote\n the development of medium to high residential densities, not to exceed eight (8) dwelling\n units per net acre. The district is intended to accommodate residential infill development\n in the older Kuna neighborhoods and in areas adjacent to light commercial activity.\n A district requirement is connection to public sewer and water. The R-8 zone is intended\n to accommodate single-family dwellings, duplexes, multifamily, manufactured homes\n and group living arrangements. There is an opportunity to initiate mixed-use activity\n in this zone through the PUD process. This district is an appropriate designation\n for a neighborhood center to be established.\n

\n

\n High density residential district (R-12): The purpose of the R-12 district is to promote\n development of higher residential development densities, not to exceed twelve (12)\n dwelling units per net acre. The R-12 zone is intended to serve, in part, as a transitional\n buffer between less intensive residential and more intensive commercial uses, as well\n as to accommodate the placement of higher density development in select areas of the\n city. A district requirement is connection to public sewer and water. The zone is\n intended to accommodate multifamily dwellings and group living arrangements. There\n is an opportunity to initiate mixed-use activity in this zone through the PUD process.\n This district is an appropriate designation for a neighborhood center to be established.\n

\n

\n High density multifamily residential district (R-20): The purpose of the R-20 district\n is to define a maximum residential density limit per acre based on factors such as\n traffic generation, availability of city services and land use compatibility. Accordingly,\n the district is established to serve higher density, multi-storied residential development,\n not to exceed twenty (20) dwelling units per net acre. District requirements include\n direct access to arterial or collector roadways and connection to public sewer and\n water. This zone is intended to accommodate multi-storied, multifamily dwellings and\n group living arrangements. There is an opportunity to initiate mixed-use activity\n in this zone through the PUD process. This district is an appropriate designation\n for a neighborhood center to be established.\n

\n \n

\n C.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Commercial:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Neighborhood commercial district (C-1): The purpose of the C-1 district is to accommodate\n a wide variety of low impact commercial activities to meet the daily needs of nearby\n neighborhood residents. This district is an appropriate designation for a neighborhood\n center and mixed-use to be established.\n

\n

\n Area commercial district (C-2): The purpose of the C-2 district is to promote the\n establishment of general business uses that are larger in scale than found in the\n neighborhood commercial district. The commercial development should have direct access\n to collector or arterial roadways. This district is an appropriate designation for\n a neighborhood center and mixed-use to be established.\n

\n

\n Service commercial district (C-3): The purpose of the C-3 district is to promote the\n development of more intensive larger scale commercial use activities with the ability\n to directly access collector or arterial roadways. The district is also established\n to address the needs of large space users whose customers make frequent purchases.\n The activities of the service commercial district are more intensive in character\n than those found in other commercial zones and may include business activities that\n are semi-industrial in nature. This district is an appropriate designation for a community\n commercial to be established.\n

\n

\n Central business district (CBD): The CBD district is established to promote development\n expansion and urban renewal in Kuna's downtown areas. The district is poised to accommodate\n a variety of business, institutional, public, quasi-public, cultural, residential\n and other related uses to create a mix of activities necessary to sustain a viable\n downtown.\n

\n

\n D.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Office district (O): The O district is established to accommodate professional, research, executive, administrative,\n accounting and similar type uses in an open and attractive industrial park-type setting\n or as a stand-alone operation. A district requirement is direct access to functionally\n classified roadways and noting these types of business uses typically generate large\n volumes of traffic. The O district is designed, in part, to act as a buffer between\n high density residential uses and commercial type enterprises. This district is an\n appropriate designation for a neighborhood center to be established. This district\n is an appropriate designation for mixed-use general or mixed-use city center to be\n established.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n E.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Manufacturing/industrial:\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Light manufacturing/industrial district (M-1): The M-1 district is established to\n promote the development of manufacturing and wholesale business operations that are\n clean, quiet and free of hazardous or objectionable elements such as noise, odor,\n dust, smoke or glare. The manufacturer is expected to operate the business enterprise\n entirely within enclosed structures and design the operation to accommodate industrial\n type traffic and loading demands. The manufacturing site is expected to be attractively\n designed and preferably constructed in a business park-like setting. Research activities\n are encouraged in this district. This district is intended to serve as a transitional\n buffer between heavy type manufacturing uses and less intense commercial and industrial\n type uses.\n

\n

\n Heavy manufacturing/industrial district (M-2): The M-2 district is intended to accommodate\n manufacturing processes and warehouse activities. Businesses locating in this district\n may produce objectionable or hazardous noise, odor, dust, smoke and glare. Therefore,\n the district is not intended for general public access due to the exposure risks.\n The manufacture business is expected to operate entirely within enclosed structures\n that are designed to accommodate industrial type traffic and loading demands. The\n M-3 district, which is limited to mining uses, has been consolidated with the M-2\n district.\n

\n

\n F.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Public district (P): The purpose of the P district is to accommodate the placement of public or quasi-public\n facilities such as schools, parks, greenbelts, cemeteries, post offices, fire stations,\n administrative and cultural buildings that are necessary to the community's advancement.\n This district is an appropriate designation for a neighborhood center and mixed-use\n to be established.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n G.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Highway overlay district: The purpose of this overlay district is to improve safety conditions, reduce congestion\n and delays, sustain traffic speeds, provide property owners with safe access to Highway\n 69, Kuna Mora Road and other roadways that assume this overlay district status. The\n overlay district has also been established to promote desirable land use development\n patterns, to include aesthetic considerations. Roadways included in this district\n are intended to serve, in part, as Kuna's gateway scenic corridors for public presentation\n purposes.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n H.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n Design review overlay district (DR): The DR district is intended to guide the general appearance of buildings as they\n are constructed or reconstructed, consistent with the goals and objectives found in\n the city's comprehensive land use plan or other development plans that have been adopted\n by the city council. The DR district is superimposed over other districts to assure\n a consistent continuity of design integrity. The design review overlay district includes\n the entire city limits and any land annexed into the city. The design character of\n the overlay district is guided by a design review committee.\n

\n \t\t\n

\n (Ord. No. 2024-06, § 2, 4-16-2024)\n
